items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mid Term Papers/Mid Term 2024 Sem 2 Set A.pdf
items.question_md: Derive the equation for relation between Shear Force and Bending Moment with suitable sketches.
items.answer_md:
**Sketch:** an element of length $\delta x$ cut from a beam carrying a UDL $w$; SF $V$ and BM $M$ on the left face, $V+\delta V$ and $M+\delta M$ on the right face, load $w\,\delta x$ at the centre.

Taking moments about the right face:
$$M + V\,\delta x - w\,\delta x\frac{\delta x}{2} - (M + \delta M) = 0$$
Neglecting $(\delta x)^2$: $\delta M = V\,\delta x$, so
$$\frac{dM}{dx} = V$$
The rate of change of BM equals the SF; therefore **BM is maximum where SF is zero**. (Vertical equilibrium also gives $dV/dx = -w$.)

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mid Term Papers/Mid Term 2024 Sem 2 Set A.pdf
items.question_md:
Draw shear force and bending moment diagrams with all significant points for the beam loaded as shown in figure.

[Figure: Beam ABCDE with A a free end, hinged support at B and roller support at E. AB = 2 m, BC = 4 m, CD = 1 m, DE = 1 m. Uniformly distributed load of 2 kN/m from A to C. Clockwise couple of 24 kN-m applied at D.]
items.answer_md:
Take $x$ from A: B at 2 m, C at 6 m, D at 7 m, E at 8 m. Hinge at B, roller at E. UDL 2 kN/m on AC; clockwise couple 24 kN·m at D.

**Reactions**

UDL $= 2 \times 6 = 12$ kN at $x = 3$ m.

$\sum M_B = 0:\; 6R_E = 12(3 - 2) + 24 = 36 \Rightarrow R_E = 6$ kN

$R_B = 12 - 6 = 6$ kN (horizontal reaction at B is zero)

**Shear force**

| Point | SF left (kN) | SF right (kN) |
|---|---|---|
| A | 0 | 0 |
| B | $-4$ | $-4 + 6 = 2$ |
| C | $2 - 8 = -6$ | $-6$ |
| D | $-6$ | $-6$ |
| E | $-6$ | 0 |

SF is zero in BC at $x = 2 + 2/2 = 3$ m.

**Bending moment**

- $M_A = 0$
- $M_B = -2(2)^2/2 = -4$ kN·m
- At $x = 3$ m: $M = 6(1) - 2(3)^2/2 = -3$ kN·m (local peak, still hogging)
- $M_C = 6(4) - 12(3) = -12$ kN·m
- $M_{D^-} = -12 - 6(1) = -18$ kN·m (maximum hogging)
- $M_{D^+} = -18 + 24 = +6$ kN·m (maximum sagging)
- $M_E = 0$

**Point of contraflexure:** the BM changes sign only through the jump at D, so **D (7 m from A)** is the point of contraflexure.

BMD: parabola from 0 at A to $-4$ at B, parabola to $-3$ at 3 m and down to $-12$ at C, straight line to $-18$ at D, vertical jump to $+6$, straight line to 0 at E.

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mid Term Papers/Mid Term 2024 Sem 2 Set B.pdf
items.topic: Composition of concurrent forces in a plane
items.question_md: Forces of 7, 1, 1 and 3 N respectively act at one of the angular points of regular pentagon towards the four other points, taken in order. Find the magnitude and direction of their resultant force.
items.answer_md:
**Given:** regular pentagon ABCDE; forces 7, 1, 1, 3 N act at A towards B, C, D, E.

**Geometry:** interior angle of a regular pentagon $=108^\circ$; the diagonals AC and AD divide it into three equal angles of $36^\circ$. Taking AB as the x-axis, the forces act at $0^\circ$, $36^\circ$, $72^\circ$, $108^\circ$.

**Resolving:**
$$\Sigma F_x=7+1\cos36^\circ+1\cos72^\circ+3\cos108^\circ=7+0.809+0.309-0.927=7.191\ \text{N}$$
$$\Sigma F_y=0+1\sin36^\circ+1\sin72^\circ+3\sin108^\circ=0.588+0.951+2.853=4.392\ \text{N}$$

**Resultant:**
$$R=\sqrt{7.191^2+4.392^2}=\mathbf{8.43\ N}$$
$$\theta=\tan^{-1}\frac{4.392}{7.191}=\mathbf{31.42^\circ}\ \text{with AB (the 7 N force), towards AC}$$

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mid Term Papers/Mid Term 2024 Sem 2 Set B.pdf
items.topic: Vector representation of forces and moments
items.question_md: Prove, "The algebraic sum of the moments of two forces about any point in their plane is equal to the moment of their resultant about that point".
items.answer_md:
**To prove:** $M_O(P) + M_O(Q) = M_O(R)$ (Varignon's theorem for two forces).

**Proof:** Let P and Q act at point A and R be their resultant (parallelogram ABCD: AB = P, AD = Q, diagonal AC = R). Take any point O in the plane, and take the x-axis along AO and let P, Q, R make angles $\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta$ with it. The moment of a force at A about O is $AO \times$ (its component perpendicular to AO):
$$M_P = AO\cdot P\sin\theta_1,\quad M_Q = AO\cdot Q\sin\theta_2,\quad M_R = AO\cdot R\sin\theta$$
The component of R perpendicular to AO equals the sum of those of P and Q: $R\sin\theta = P\sin\theta_1 + Q\sin\theta_2$. Multiplying by AO: $M_R = M_P + M_Q$. Hence proved.

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mid Term Papers/Mid Term 2024 Sem 2 Set B.pdf
items.topic: Reduction of a force system to a force and a couple
items.question_md:
Explain the properties of couple and replace the 500N force by 1) A force through A and couple 2) A force through B and a couple.

[Figure: Horizontal cantilever fixed at B (left wall), extending 6 cm to A; from A an arm bends down and extends a further 4 cm horizontally to the right, where a vertical downward load of 500 N acts at the end.]
items.answer_md:
**Properties of a couple:**
1. Two equal, opposite, parallel, non-collinear forces; their resultant force is zero, so a couple produces only rotation.
2. Its moment $M = F \times d$ is the same about every point in its plane.
3. A couple cannot be balanced by a single force, only by an equal and opposite couple.
4. It can be moved anywhere in its plane, or to a parallel plane, without changing its effect.

**Replacing the 500 N load** (it acts 4 cm to the right of A horizontally, so 6 + 4 = 10 cm from B; the vertical offset does not matter for a vertical force):

1. **At A:** 500 N downward at A **plus** a clockwise couple $500 \times 4 = 2000$ N·cm = **20 N·m**.
2. **At B:** 500 N downward at B **plus** a clockwise couple $500 \times 10 = 5000$ N·cm = **50 N·m**.

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mid Term Papers/Mid Term 2024 Sem 2 Set B.pdf
items.topic: Equilibrium of rigid bodies in two and three dimensions
items.question_md: Explain determinate and indeterminate beams with example.
items.answer_md:
**Statically determinate beam:** the number of unknown reactions does not exceed the available equations of static equilibrium ($\Sigma F_x=0$, $\Sigma F_y=0$, $\Sigma M=0$), so all reactions can be found from statics alone. *Examples:* simply supported beam, cantilever, overhanging beam.

**Statically indeterminate beam:** the unknown reactions exceed the equations of statics, so extra (compatibility/deflection) conditions are needed. *Examples:* fixed (built-in at both ends) beam, propped cantilever, continuous beam.

items.topic: Equilibrium of rigid bodies in two and three dimensions
items.question_md:
Calculate support reactions for the following beam;

[Figure: Beam AB, hinged at A, roller at B on a plane inclined with slope 1 (vertical) : 2 (horizontal). A 100 kN inclined point load at 60° acts at 1 m from A. From 1 m to 2 m a triangular load (varying up to 5 kN/m at 2 m) acts; a uniformly distributed load of 50 kN/m acts from 1 m to B. Spans: 1 m, 1 m, 2 m.]
items.answer_md:
**Given:** AB = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4 m; A hinged; B roller on a plane of slope 1 (V) : 2 (H), so the plane is at $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(1/2)=26.57^\circ$ and $R_B$ (normal to it) is at $26.57^\circ$ to the vertical. 100 kN at $60^\circ$ (to the beam) at 1 m; triangular load 0 to 5 kN/m from 1 m to 2 m; UDL 50 kN/m from 1 m to B.

**Step 1: Equivalent loads**
- 100 kN: vertical $100\sin60^\circ=86.60$ kN at 1 m; horizontal $100\cos60^\circ=50$ kN
- Triangle: $\frac12\times1\times5=2.5$ kN at $1+\frac23=1.667$ m
- UDL: $50\times3=150$ kN at $1+1.5=2.5$ m

**Step 2: $\Sigma M_A=0$**
$$R_B\cos26.57^\circ\times4=86.60(1)+2.5(1.667)+150(2.5)=465.77$$
$$R_B\cos26.57^\circ=116.44\ \text{kN}\Rightarrow R_B=\frac{116.44}{0.8944}=\mathbf{130.19\ kN}$$
Horizontal component of $R_B$: $130.19\sin26.57^\circ=58.22$ kN.

**Step 3: $\Sigma F_y=0$**
$$V_A=86.60+2.5+150-116.44=\mathbf{122.66\ kN}\ (\uparrow)$$

**Step 4: $\Sigma F_x=0$** (taking the 50 kN horizontal component towards B and the horizontal component of $R_B$ towards A, as for a plane rising towards B)
$$H_A=58.22-50=\mathbf{8.22\ kN}$$
*(If the figure shows the horizontal components in the same sense, $H_A=58.22+50=108.22$ kN; $R_B$ and $V_A$ are unchanged.)*

**Step 5: Resultant at A**
$$R_A=\sqrt{122.66^2+8.22^2}=\mathbf{122.94\ kN}\ \text{at }86.17^\circ\text{ to the horizontal}$$

**Answer:** $R_B=130.19$ kN normal to the inclined plane; $V_A=122.66$ kN, $H_A=8.22$ kN, $R_A=122.94$ kN.

items.question_md:
Draw the shear force and bending momemt diagram for the following beam:

[Figure: Beam ABCD, hinged at A, roller at D. UDL 20 kN/m over AB (2 m); clockwise couple 200 kN-m at B; at C (3 m from B) a 40 kN downward point load and a 100 kN-m couple; CD = 3 m.]
items.answer_md:
Take $x$ from A: B at 2 m, C at 5 m, D at 8 m. Hinge at A, roller at D. Both couples taken **clockwise** (the figure description does not give the sense of the 100 kN·m couple).

**Reactions**

$\sum M_A = 0:\; 8R_D = 40(1) + 200 + 40(5) + 100 = 540 \Rightarrow R_D = 67.5$ kN

$R_A = 40 + 40 - 67.5 = 12.5$ kN

**SF:** $+12.5$ at A, falling linearly to $12.5 - 40 = -27.5$ at B (zero at $x = 0.625$ m), constant $-27.5$ to C, drops to $-67.5$ at C, constant to D.

**BM:**
- $M_A = 0$; at $x = 0.625$ m: $M = 3.91$ kN·m
- $M_{B^-} = 12.5(2) - 40(1) = -15$ kN·m; $M_{B^+} = -15 + 200 = 185$ kN·m
- $M_{C^-} = 185 - 27.5(3) = 102.5$ kN·m; $M_{C^+} = 102.5 + 100 = 202.5$ kN·m
- $M_D = 0$ (check: $67.5 \times 3 = 202.5$)

**Maximum BM = 202.5 kN·m just right of C.** Contraflexure at $x = 1.25$ m ($12.5x - 10x^2 = 0$) and through the jump at B.

Determine the forces in each member of the truss as shown in fig.

[Figure: Truss with bottom chord A–B–C–D–E (supports at A and E) and top joints H, G, I; members AH, HG, GI, IE, HB, GB, GC, GD, ID, and bottom chord members. Loads 6 kN at B, 7 kN at C, 4 kN at D. Heights shown as 3 m and 4.5 m; span 12 m, 4 @ 3 m.]

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mini Test Papers/Mini Test 2020-21 Sem 1.pdf
items.topic: Equilibrium of rigid bodies in two and three dimensions
items.question_md:
A 10 kg ring is supported by a smooth surface at E and a wire AB. A body of mass 3 kg is fixed at D as shown in the figure below. What is the tension in the wire AB? Also find angle $\alpha$. The point A is directly above the point O.

[Figure: Ring of radius 2 m with centre O. Wire AB runs from point A at the top of the ring up to a fixed support B, making angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal at A. Point D is on the ring at $45^\circ$ above the horizontal through O, with the 3 kg body attached at D. The ring rests at E against a smooth inclined surface that makes $60^\circ$ with the horizontal at its base. A is directly above O.]
items.answer_md:
**Given:** ring mass 10 kg (weight $10 \times 9.81 = 98.1$ N at O), radius 2 m; body 3 kg ($3 \times 9.81 = 29.43$ N) at D, $45^\circ$ above the horizontal through O; smooth surface at E inclined at $60^\circ$; wire AB at angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal at A, A vertically above O.

### 1. Key observation
The reaction at a smooth contact is normal to the surface; for a ring the normal passes through the centre O. So $R_E$ and the ring's own weight both pass through O, and $R_E$ makes $60^\circ$ with the vertical.

### 2. Moments about O
Arm of the 29.43 N load $= 2\cos45^\circ = 1.414$ m. Only the horizontal component of T has a moment about O (its vertical component passes through O), arm = OA = 2 m:
$$T\cos\alpha \times 2 = 29.43 \times 1.414 = 41.62 \Rightarrow T\cos\alpha = 20.81\ \text{N}$$

### 3. Horizontal equilibrium
$$R_E\sin60^\circ = T\cos\alpha = 20.81 \Rightarrow R_E = 24.03\ \text{N}$$

### 4. Vertical equilibrium
$$T\sin\alpha + R_E\cos60^\circ = 98.1 + 29.43 = 127.53$$
$$T\sin\alpha = 127.53 - 12.01 = 115.52\ \text{N}$$

### 5. Result
$$T = \sqrt{20.81^2 + 115.52^2} = \mathbf{117.37\ N}$$
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}\frac{115.52}{20.81} = \mathbf{79.79^\circ}$$

**Answer:** tension in AB = 117.37 N at $\alpha = 79.79^\circ$ to the horizontal; reaction at E = 24.03 N.

items.topic: Reduction of a force system to a force and a couple
items.question_md:
Determine magnitude and direction of minimum force P, so that resultant of system is passing through point 'D'.

[Figure: Regular hexagon ABCDEF with side ED = 0.3 m and AB as the top side. Force P acts at A, inclined at angle $\alpha$ to AB. A force of 400 N acts vertically upward at C. A downward vertical force of unspecified magnitude acts at F.]
items.answer_md:
**Given:** regular hexagon ABCDEF, side $a = 0.3$ m, AB at the top; 400 N upward at C; a vertical downward force (call it $F$) at F; P at A inclined at $\alpha$ to AB. The magnitude of the force at F is not readable in the figure, so the result is given in terms of $F$.

### 1. Condition
The resultant passes through D when $\sum M_D = 0$.

### 2. Geometry (centre at the origin)
A$(-0.15,\ 0.26)$, B$(0.15,\ 0.26)$, C$(0.3,\ 0)$, D$(0.15,\ -0.26)$, F$(-0.3,\ 0)$.
- Horizontal distance of C from D $= 0.15$ m
- Horizontal distance of F from D $= 0.45$ m
- AD is a long diagonal: $AD = 2a = 0.6$ m, inclined at $60^\circ$ to AB.

### 3. Moments about D (anticlockwise positive)
- 400 N ↑ at C: $+400 \times 0.15 = +60$ N·m
- $F$ ↓ at F (left of D): $+0.45F$ N·m

P must supply an equal clockwise moment: $P \times d_P = 60 + 0.45F$.

### 4. Minimum P
For a given moment, P is least when its arm about D is the greatest, i.e. when **P is perpendicular to AD**, giving $d_P = AD = 0.6$ m:
$$P_{min} = \frac{60 + 0.45F}{0.6} = \mathbf{100 + 0.75F\ \ (N)}$$

### 5. Direction
AD makes $60^\circ$ with AB, so P perpendicular to AD makes $\alpha = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = \mathbf{30^\circ}$ with AB, pointing upward and towards B (this sense gives the clockwise moment about D).

Substitute the value of the downward force at F from the figure into $P_{min} = 100 + 0.75F$ (if there were no force at F, $P_{min} = 100$ N).

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mini Test Papers/Mini Test 2020-21 Sem 1.pdf
items.topic: Centroid of areas
items.question_md:
Determine centroid of shaded area with respect to the given axis.

[Figure: Shaded trapezium ABED, symmetric about the y-axis, with origin O at the bottom. Lines OA and OB each make $60^\circ$ with the x-axis. DE is a horizontal line at height $a$ above O and AB is a horizontal line at height $b$ above O. M is the midpoint of AB and N is the midpoint of DE, both on the y-axis. The shaded area lies between DE and AB.]
items.answer_md:
By symmetry about the y-axis, $\bar x=0$. Since OA and OB make $60^\circ$ with the x-axis, the half-width at height $y$ is $y\cot60^\circ=y/\sqrt3$, so a strip has $dA=\frac{2y}{\sqrt3}dy$.

$$A=\int_a^b\frac{2y}{\sqrt3}dy=\frac{b^2-a^2}{\sqrt3},\qquad \int y\,dA=\frac{2(b^3-a^3)}{3\sqrt3}$$
$$\bar y=\frac{2(b^3-a^3)}{3(b^2-a^2)}=\mathbf{\frac{2(a^2+ab+b^2)}{3(a+b)}}\ \text{above O},\qquad \bar x=0$$

items.topic: Equilibrium of rigid bodies in two and three dimensions
items.question_md: Define the term 'Support reaction'?
items.answer_md: **Support reaction:** the reactive force (and moment, at a fixed support) developed by a support on a structure to resist the applied loads and keep it in equilibrium. Example: for a simply supported beam the upward forces $R_A$ and $R_B$ at the supports are the support reactions.

items.question_md:
Calculate the support reaction for the beam given below.

[Figure: Simply supported beam AB of span 5 m, supported at A and B. Point loads of 3 kN at 2 m from A, 4 kN at a further 1 m (3 m from A), and 5 kN at a further 2 m (5 m from A).]
items.answer_md:
**Given:** span 5 m; 3 kN at 2 m, 4 kN at 3 m and 5 kN at 5 m from A.

$\sum M_A = 0$:
$$R_B \times 5 = 3 \times 2 + 4 \times 3 + 5 \times 5 = 6 + 12 + 25 = 43 \Rightarrow R_B = \mathbf{8.6\ kN}$$
$\sum F_y = 0$:
$$R_A = (3 + 4 + 5) - 8.6 = \mathbf{3.4\ kN}$$
(The 5 kN load acts directly over B and is carried wholly by B.)

items.question_md:
A simply supported beam, AB of span 6 m is loaded as shown in figure below. Determine the support reactions.

[Figure: Simply supported beam AB of span 6 m with reactions $R_A$ at A and $R_B$ at B. Segments: A to C = 1.5 m, C to E = 1.5 m, E to D = 1.5 m, D to B = 1.5 m. Point load 4 kN at C, uniformly distributed load 2 kN/m from C to E, point load 1.5 kN at D.]

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mini Test Papers/Mini Test 2020-21 Sem 2.pdf
items.question_md: Define Bending moment and Shear force?
items.answer_md:
**Shear force** at a section is the algebraic sum of all vertical forces (loads and reactions) acting on either side of the section (unit: kN).

**Bending moment** at a section is the algebraic sum of the moments, about that section, of all forces acting on either side of it (unit: kN·m). Sagging BM is positive, hogging negative.

items.question_md:
Draw the shear force and bending moment diagram for the following loaded beam.

[Figure: Simply supported beam AB of span 4.0 m with supports at A and B. Point load 6.0 kN at 1.0 m from A. Point C at 2.0 m from A. Uniformly distributed load 2.0 kN/m over the last 2.0 m to B; a dimension of 0.5 m is marked between C and a point just right of C.]
items.answer_md:
Simply supported beam AB, span 4 m. Take $x$ from A: 6 kN at 1 m; UDL 2 kN/m from C ($x = 2$ m) to B.

**Reactions**

UDL $= 2 \times 2 = 4$ kN at $x = 3$ m.

$\sum M_A = 0:\; 4R_B = 6(1) + 4(3) = 18 \Rightarrow R_B = 4.5$ kN; $R_A = 10 - 4.5 = 5.5$ kN

**SF:** $+5.5$ from A to the load; $5.5 - 6 = -0.5$ from the load to C; then linear from $-0.5$ to $-4.5$ at B.

**BM:**
- $M_A = 0$
- At the load (1 m): $5.5 \times 1 = 5.5$ kN·m (**maximum**, SF changes sign)
- $M_C = 5.5(2) - 6(1) = 5.0$ kN·m
- $M_B = 0$

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mini Test Papers/Mini Test 2021-22.pdf
items.topic: Composition of concurrent forces in a plane
items.question_md: State and Explain parallelogram law of forces?
items.answer_md:
**Statement:** If two forces acting at a point are represented in magnitude and direction by the two adjacent sides of a parallelogram, their resultant is represented in magnitude and direction by the diagonal of the parallelogram through that point.

For forces P and Q at angle $\theta$:
$$R=\sqrt{P^2+Q^2+2PQ\cos\theta},\qquad \tan\alpha=\frac{Q\sin\theta}{P+Q\cos\theta}$$
where $\alpha$ is the angle of R with P.

**Explanation:** in parallelogram OACB, OA = P, OB = Q; drop CD perpendicular to OA produced. Then $AD=Q\cos\theta$, $CD=Q\sin\theta$, and from right triangle OCD, $R^2=(P+Q\cos\theta)^2+(Q\sin\theta)^2$, which gives the result.

items.topic: Vector representation of forces and moments
items.question_md: What are the the various characteristics of a force?
items.answer_md:
A force is completely defined by its characteristics:
1. **Magnitude** (e.g. 50 N)
2. **Direction**, the inclination of its line of action
3. **Sense**: push or pull, shown by the arrowhead
4. **Point of application** on the body

items.path: library/archive/CE1103/Previous Year Mini Test Papers/Mini Test 2021-22.pdf
items.topic: Planar force systems
items.question_md: A square ABCD of 60mm side is subjected to force of 10 N, 20 N, 30 N and 40 N along the sides AB, AC, BD and AD respectively. Find magnitude, direction and position of the resultant force with respect to A.
items.answer_md:
**Axes:** A(0, 0), B(60, 0), C(60, 60), D(0, 60) mm. Diagonal forces resolve at $45^\circ$ ($\cos45^\circ = 0.7071$).

| Force | Line | $F_x$ (N) | $F_y$ (N) | Moment about A (N·mm, +ve anticlockwise) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 N | A→B | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| 20 N | A→C | 14.142 | 14.142 | 0 |
| 30 N | B→D | −21.213 | 21.213 | $21.213 \times 60 = 1272.79$ |
| 40 N | A→D | 0 | 40 | 0 |
| **Sum** | | **2.929** | **75.355** | **1272.79** |

**Magnitude:**
$$R = \sqrt{2.929^2 + 75.355^2} = \mathbf{75.41\ N}$$
**Direction:**
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}\frac{75.355}{2.929} = \mathbf{87.77^\circ}\ \text{with AB (acting upward, slightly towards B)}$$
**Position with respect to A:** perpendicular distance $d = 1272.79/75.41 = \mathbf{16.88\ mm}$. The resultant cuts AB at
$$x = \frac{1272.79}{75.355} = \mathbf{16.89\ mm\ from\ A}$$

items.topic: Reduction of a force system to a force and a couple
items.question_md:
Determine the resultant of the system of forces and moment acting on a lamina as shown in figure. Also locate the points of intersection of the resultant with the arm AB, BC and CD of the lamina.

[Figure: L-shaped lamina with vertical arm AB (A at top, B at bottom, AB = 1.5 m), horizontal arm BC (BC = 2 m), and vertical arm CD going down from C (CD = 1 m). A couple of 75 N-m acts at A. A 100 N force acts vertically downward at C. A 75 N force acts at B, directed upward at $30^\circ$ to the vertical. A 50 N horizontal force acts to the right at D.]
items.answer_md:
**Reading of the figure (assumptions):** B(0, 0) at the corner; A(0, 1.5) above B; C(2, 0); D(2, −1) below C. The 75 N force at B points upward and to the right at $30^\circ$ to the vertical; the 75 N·m couple at A is anticlockwise.

### 1. Resolution of forces
| Force | Point | $F_x$ (N) | $F_y$ (N) | Moment about B (N·m, +ve anticlockwise) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 75 N at $30^\circ$ to vertical | B (0, 0) | $75\sin30^\circ = 37.50$ | $75\cos30^\circ = 64.95$ | 0 |
| 100 N ↓ | C (2, 0) | 0 | −100 | $2 \times (-100) = -200$ |
| 50 N → | D (2, −1) | 50 | 0 | $-(-1)(50) = +50$ |
| Couple | A | 0 | 0 | +75 |
| **Sum** | | **87.50** | **−35.05** | **−75** |

### 2. Resultant
$$R = \sqrt{87.50^2 + 35.05^2} = \mathbf{94.26\ N}$$
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}\frac{35.05}{87.50} = \mathbf{21.83^\circ}\ \text{below the horizontal, acting to the right}$$
$\sum M_B = 75$ N·m clockwise, so the perpendicular distance from B is $d = 75/94.26 = 0.796$ m.

### 3. Equation of the line of action
For any point $(x, y)$ on it: $xR_y - yR_x = \sum M_B$
$$-35.05x - 87.50y = -75$$

### 4. Points of intersection
- **With AB** ($x = 0$): $y = 75/87.50 = \mathbf{0.857\ m}$ above B (0.643 m below A), within AB.
- **With BC** ($y = 0$): $x = 75/35.05 = \mathbf{2.14\ m}$ from B, i.e. on BC produced, 0.14 m beyond C.
- **With CD** ($x = 2$): $y = (75 - 70.10)/87.50 = \mathbf{0.056\ m}$ above C, i.e. on DC produced, 0.056 m above C.

If the couple in your figure is clockwise, $\sum M_B = -225$ N·m; repeat steps 3 and 4 with 225 in place of 75.

items.topic: Equilibrium of rigid bodies in two and three dimensions
items.question_md:
Determine the reactions at A, B, C and D for the system of forces loaded as shown in figure.

[Figure: Horizontal beam AB with a hinged support at A. A vertical load of 300 kN acts 1 m from A, and B is a further 2 m to the right (AB = 3 m). End B of the beam rests on an inclined member CD through rollers. Member CD is hinged at C at the bottom and inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. At its upper end D it is supported by rollers against a vertical wall. Along CD the distance from C to the contact point under B is 1.05 m, and from that point to D is 1.45 m.]
items.answer_md:
**Given:** beam AB, hinge at A, 300 kN at 1 m from A, AB = 3 m. B rests on rollers on member CD, which is hinged at C, inclined at $30^\circ$ and rests on rollers against a vertical wall at D. CB = 1.05 m, BD = 1.45 m along CD (CD = 2.5 m).

### 1. FBD of beam AB
A roller reaction is normal to the surface it rolls on. CD is at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, so $R_B$ is perpendicular to CD, i.e. at $30^\circ$ to the vertical.

$\sum M_A = 0$:
$$R_B\cos30^\circ \times 3 = 300 \times 1 \Rightarrow R_B = \frac{100}{0.866} = \mathbf{115.47\ kN}$$
Components: vertical $R_B\cos30^\circ = 100$ kN, horizontal $R_B\sin30^\circ = 57.74$ kN (towards A, CD rising towards the wall at D).

$\sum F_x = 0$: $H_A = 57.74$ kN (away from B)

$\sum F_y = 0$: $V_A = 300 - 100 = 200$ kN

$$R_A = \sqrt{200^2 + 57.74^2} = \mathbf{208.17\ kN},\quad \theta = \tan^{-1}\frac{200}{57.74} = 73.9^\circ\ \text{to the horizontal}$$

### 2. FBD of member CD
Forces: $R_B = 115.47$ kN pressing on CD (normal to it) at 1.05 m from C; $R_D$ horizontal (wall rollers) at D; $R_C$ at hinge C.

Height of D above C $= 2.5\sin30^\circ = 1.25$ m. $R_B$ is normal to CD, so its arm about C is 1.05 m.

$\sum M_C = 0$:
$$R_D \times 1.25 = 115.47 \times 1.05 \Rightarrow R_D = \mathbf{97.0\ kN}\ \text{(horizontal)}$$

$\sum F_x = 0$: $H_C = 97.0 - 57.74 = 39.26$ kN

$\sum F_y = 0$: $V_C = 100$ kN

$$R_C = \sqrt{39.26^2 + 100^2} = \mathbf{107.43\ kN},\quad \theta = \tan^{-1}\frac{100}{39.26} = 68.6^\circ\ \text{to the horizontal}$$

**Answer:** $R_A = 208.17$ kN at $73.9^\circ$; $R_B = 115.47$ kN normal to CD; $R_C = 107.43$ kN at $68.6^\circ$; $R_D = 97.0$ kN horizontal.
